rationale: Neither candidate surfaces the ground truth's actual emphasized concerns (WebSocket native-speed rejection asymmetry, missing profiler/VRAM evidence, the talker-vs-s2mel_decoder duration_factor range mismatch, or the 4-file range duplication) — both instead find their own orthogonal issues in unseen parts of the diff, so recall is low for both. Y is more tightly grounded: its two findings quote exact code with line-range headers and are explicitly confirmed by running local tests/reproducing the bug, and one finding (talker.py 561-569 duration_factor silently ignored as a bare scalar) sits in the exact code region GT's reviewers flagged, showing closer thematic engagement even though it's a different specific bug. X offers broader, well-reasoned coverage (7 substantive findings plus scope/minor notes) and correctly calls out the visible XPU/Docker version-bump scope creep, but its claims about talker.py/2.0-regression behavior are less independently verified and slightly more speculative. Both are concretely actionable with file:line references and suggested fixes.
